newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas rises again in winter in busy trade.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas rises again in winter in busy trade.

text.p: IPE natural gas prices continued their upward trend on Tuesday afternoon as winter levels firmed in another day of busy trade.

Every month from September to May traded at least once, and in some cases more than once, as a total of 325 lots was done. Although September, October and March prices slipped, the heart of the winter from November to February was stronger.

February gained the most, settling at 18.30 pence a therm, a rise of 0.20 pence on the day. But December and January were nearly as strong, rising by 0.175 pence each to settle at 15.475 pence and 18.225 pence respectively.
The fourth quarter settled at 13.41 pence on the IPE, and Q1 98 at 16.94 pence. The Q4 figure is within the assessed range for the OTC market from Monday, but Q1 is higher.
Only three months, August, June and July were untraded by the close. Front month August was bid at 9.60 pence and offered at 9.70 pence, while outer month July 98 has yet to see its first deal.
Tuesday is the seventh successive day on which the IPE has seen busy trade, after a long period when deals were sporadic and completely blank days were commonplace.
